tool_observations: Shell-launched M3 executable ad1fa8f02f75cbc1a62bea10d0bb90795aa962a0562db28e098e8bb1d6c05267: bulk type_text MORGAN produced no text; an ordinary m key appeared and began search.

In that shell-launched process, Ctrl+A visibly selected the invented Unicode string; Ctrl+C, BackSpace, Ctrl+V left search empty.

M4 same-binary comparison: after closing the shell-launched process, sky.launch_app opened the executable directly. Accessibility set_value prepared ZÁRATE, ZOË 李; Ctrl+A, Ctrl+C, BackSpace, Ctrl+V restored the exact Unicode string and began the matching search.

Final build 11ac4dac9afedbcdef1389af74e763eaf7958749cade54a6027c150c8f0cca7e, native app-launcher launch: Ctrl+A, Ctrl+C, BackSpace, Ctrl+V again restored exactly ZÁRATE, ZOË 李 in patient search. This final-build observation is distinct from accessibility value replacement used to prepare the source string.
source_findings: Cached winit Windows keyboard.rs 168 onward discards WM_CHAR/WM_SYSCHAR when no matching key event exists. This is a plausible explanation for bulk tool text, not verified tool internals.

Cached i-slint-backend-winit clipboard.rs creates a Windows arboard clipboard. Backend clipboard get/set swallow errors. arboard 3.7.0 Windows initialization succeeds directly; opening the OS clipboard can fail after bounded retries.
conclusion: Clipboard failure is launch-dependent in the observed comparison. The tool-shell launch environment is the likely cause; the exact OS restriction was not instrumented. No application input-code workaround or security-setting change was made. The user also confirmed that manual paste now works after the native relaunch.
limits: Physical IME composition, dead keys, keyboard layouts, and full assistive-technology behavior are unverified.
Successful accessibility value replacement is not native typing or paste.
build_difference: Final build adds Notes keyboard focus correction and expands callback checks; input/clipboard implementation and dependencies are unchanged.
